author: copilot
body:
Implements a production-ready Next.js 14 application for managing academic research with AI-powered features, multi-source paper search, and citation management.

## Core Infrastructure

- **Next.js 14 + TypeScript**: App Router with server/client components, strict type checking
- **Authentication**: NextAuth.js with credentials provider, bcryptjs password hashing, JWT sessions
- **Database**: Prisma ORM with PostgreSQL schema (8 models: User, Paper, Collection, CollectionPaper, Annotation, InsightCard, Citation, Document)
- **UI Framework**: Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui components (Radix UI primitives)

## Feature Implementation

### Paper Search & Discovery
- Multi-source search across 200M+ papers (Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, Crossref APIs)
- Smart deduplication logic matching by DOI and normalized title
- Save functionality with full metadata preservation
- Advanced filtering (year range, citations, venue)

### Paper Management
- CRUD operations with user ownership validation
- Detail view with metadata, abstract, and AI analysis
- Collections with hierarchical support (parent/child relationships)
- Annotations with highlight support and color coding

### AI Integration
- OpenAI GPT-3.5-turbo for paper summarization
- Structured extraction: methodology, findings, limitations
- Configurable token limits and model parameters
- Graceful degradation when API key unavailable

### Citation System
- Six citation styles: APA, MLA, Chicago, Harvard, IEEE, Vancouver
- BibTeX export with special character escaping (`escapeBibTeXValue`)
- RIS format export
- Citation generator component with copy/export UI

### Research Tools
- Insights management with Kanban-style status tracking
- Dashboard with statistics aggregation (papers, collections, insights counts)
- Research progress visualization

## API Routes

All routes implement session validation and proper error handling:

```typescript
// Example: Search endpoint with multi-source aggregation
GET /api/search?q={query}&limit={limit}&source={all|semantic-scholar|openalex|crossref}

// Papers CRUD with pagination
GET /api/papers?page={page}&perPage={perPage}
POST /api/papers

// Collections with ownership verification
POST /api/collections
DELETE /api/collections?id={id}

// AI services with fallback handling
POST /api/ai/summarize
```

## Type Safety & Error Handling

- Zod schemas for request validation on all POST/PATCH routes
- Proper `null` to `undefined` conversion for Prisma → API compatibility
- NextAuth adapter typed as `Adapter` (removed `as any`)
- Enhanced error logging with structured output for debugging

## Code Quality Improvements

Applied from code review:
- Enhanced deduplication with case-insensitive title matching
- BibTeX special character escaping function
- Extracted magic numbers to configuration constants (`MAX_FULL_TEXT_LENGTH`, `AI_MODEL`)
- JSON parse error logging with raw response output

## Documentation

- **README.md**: Installation, setup, environment configuration, project structure
- **DEPLOYMENT.md**: Four deployment options (Vercel, Railway, Docker, VPS), database hosting, security best practices
- **API.md**: Complete endpoint reference with request/response examples

body:
Implements a modern C++ class for rendering maps with GPS tracking paths to PNG using Mapnik.

## Changes

- **`src/MapPathRenderer.hpp`** - Class declaration with:
  - `TrackingPoint` struct (lon, lat, timestamp)
  - Non-copyable, movable design
  - Methods: `loadBaseLayer`, `addTrackingPath`, `addPointMarkers`, `setExtent`, `zoomToTrackingPoints`, `render`
  - Configurable font via `setFontName()`, error access via `getLastError()`

- **`src/MapPathRenderer.cpp`** - Implementation using:
  - Memory datasource for dynamic geometry
  - Coordinate transform from WGS84 → Web Mercator
  - Symbolizers: polygon (fill/stroke), line (paths), markers + text (labels)

- **`CMakeLists.txt`** - Build config using `mapnik-config`

## Usage

```cpp
ioc_earth::MapPathRenderer renderer(800, 600, "epsg:3857");
renderer.loadBaseLayer("countries.shp", "base");

std::vector<ioc_earth::TrackingPoint> track = {
    {12.4964, 41.9028, "2024-01-01 10:00"},
    {12.3155, 45.4408, "2024-01-01 14:00"}
};
renderer.addTrackingPath(track, "blue", 2.0);
renderer.addPointMarkers(track, "red", 8.0, true);
renderer.zoomToTrackingPoints(0.1);
renderer.render("output.png");
```

> 
> 1. **Dipendenze:** Deve includere tutte le intestazioni Mapnik necessarie:

>    ```cpp
>    void addTrackingPath(const std::vector<std::pair<double, double>>& coords, const std::vector<std::string>& timestamps);
>    ```
>    - Crea un **layer Mapnik in memoria** usando `memory_datasource`
>    - Disegna una **LineString** (`path`) con le `coords` come una linea rossa e spessa (es. stroke-width: 3, colore rosso)
>    - Disegna dei **Punti** (`mark`) in corrispondenza delle stesse coordinate
>    - Ogni Punto deve avere un attributo feature chiamato `"time"` contenente la stringa del `timestamp` corrispondente
>    - Applica uno stile al layer dei Punti che utilizza un **`text_symbolizer`** per etichettare i punti con il valore dell'attributo `[time]`
> 
> 5. **Metodo `renderToPng`:**
>    ```cpp
>    bool renderToPng(const std::string& output_filename, double min_lon, double min_lat, double max_lon, double max_lat);
>    ```
>    - Imposta il box di zoom (`zoom_to_box`) usando le coordinate Long/Lat fornite

>    - Salva l'output in un file PNG
>    - Ritorna `true` se il rendering ha successo
>

>     // Inizializza Mapnik
>     mapnik::datasource_cache::instance().register_datasources("/path/to/mapnik/input");

>     // Crea istanza di MapPathRenderer (800x600, EPSG:3857)
>     MapPathRenderer renderer(800, 600);
>     
>     // (Opzionale) Carica layer di base

>     
>     // Coordinate di esempio (percorso attraverso l'Italia)
>     std::vector<std::pair<double, double>> coords = {
>         {12.4964, 41.9028},  // Roma
>         {11.2558, 43.7696},  // Firenze
>         {11.3426, 44.4949},  // Bologna
>         {9.1900, 45.4642},   // Milano
>         {7.6869, 45.0703}    // Torino
>     };
>     
>     std::vector<std::string> timestamps = {
>         "2024-01-01 08:00",
>         "2024-01-01 10:30",
>         "2024-01-01 12:00",
>         "2024-01-01 15:00",
>         "2024-01-01 18:00"
>     };
>     
>     // Aggiungi il percorso di tracking
>     renderer.addTrackingPath(coords, timestamps);
>     
>     // Renderizza su PNG (bounding box Italia)
>     renderer.renderToPng("italy_track.png", 6.5, 35.5, 18.5, 47.0);
>     
>     return 0;
> }
> ```
> 
> ### 2. Aggiornare `README.md`
> Aggiornare il README esistente con:
> - Descrizione completa della libreria IOC_Earth
> - Requisiti (Mapnik, compilatore C++17)
> - Istruzioni di compilazione dettagliate
> - Esempio d'uso completo

> Creare un file CMake per la compilazione con:
> - Requisiti C++17
> - Find e link a libreria Mapnik
> - Target eseguibile
> 
> ## Note Importanti
> - L'implementazione del `memory_datasource` e del `text_symbolizer` per le etichette è il cuore del problema
> - Assicurarsi che `mapnik::datasource_cache::instance().register_datasources()` sia chiamato all'inizio

author: mpdude
body:
Symfony 8 added return types to all interfaces and classes. This leaks through the Behat API in places where Behat used classes from Symfony, for example the Event Dispatcher implementation or the `\Behat\Testwork\ServiceContainer\Extension` interface which extends `\Symfony\Component\DependencyInjection\Compiler\CompilerPassInterface`.

The Behat maintainers work on creating a new Behat release supporting Symfony 8, but it will also affect extensions like this one (https://github.com/Behat/Behat/pull/1687).

Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Validator is Vulnerable to Incomplete Filtering of One or More Instances of Special Elements

Versions of the package validator before 13.15.22 are vulnerable to Incomplete Filtering of One or More Instances of Special Elements in the isLength() function that does not take into account Unicode variation selectors (\uFE0F, \uFE0E) appearing in a sequence which lead to improper string length calculation. This can lead to an application using isLength for input validation accepting strings significantly longer than intended, resulting in issues like data truncation in databases, buffer overflows in other system components, or denial-of-service.

🚨 validator.js has a URL validation bypass vulnerability in its isURL function

A URL validation bypass vulnerability exists in validator.js prior to version 13.15.20. The isURL() function uses '://' as a delimiter to parse protocols, while browsers use ':' as the delimiter. This parsing difference allows attackers to bypass protocol and domain validation by crafting URLs leading to XSS and Open Redirect attacks.

body:
The "Show Sensors & Statistics" button failed with `AttributeError: 'SensorConfig' object has no attribute 'display_name'`. Additionally, the `feature_statistics` table remained empty despite resampling completing successfully.

## Changes

**Fixed display_name access in `/api/features/sensors_with_stats`**
- `SensorConfig` lacks `display_name`; retrieve it from `SensorDefinition` via `get_sensor_definition()`

```python
# Before
"display_name": sensor_config.display_name  # AttributeError

# After  
sensor_def = get_sensor_definition(sensor_config.category_name)
display_name = sensor_def.display_name if sensor_def else sensor_config.category_name
```

**Auto-calculate feature statistics after resampling**
- `/resample` endpoint now calls `calculate_feature_statistics()` automatically
- When `flush=true`, also flushes `feature_statistics` table before recalculation
- Errors logged but don't fail resampling request
- Response includes `feature_stats` object with calculation metrics

```python
stats = resample_all_categories(sample_rate, flush=flush)

# New: automatic feature statistics calculation

feature_stats_result = calculate_feature_statistics()

This PR updates [django](https://pypi.org/project/django) from **4.0.3** to **5.2.9**.



<details>
  <summary>Changelog</summary>
  
  
   ### 5.2.9
   ```
   ==========================

*December 2, 2025*

Django 5.2.9 fixes one security issue with severity "high", one security issue
with severity "moderate", and several bugs in 5.2.8.

CVE-2025-13372: Potential SQL injection in ``FilteredRelation`` column aliases on PostgreSQL
============================================================================================

:class:`.FilteredRelation` was subject to SQL injection in column aliases,
using a suitably crafted dictionary, with dictionary expansion, as the
``**kwargs`` passed to :meth:`.QuerySet.annotate` or :meth:`.QuerySet.alias` on
PostgreSQL.

CVE-2025-64460: Potential denial-of-service vulnerability in XML ``Deserializer``
=================================================================================

:ref:`XML Serialization <serialization-formats-xml>` was subject to a potential
denial-of-service attack due to quadratic time complexity when deserializing
crafted documents containing many nested invalid elements. The internal helper
``django.core.serializers.xml_serializer.getInnerText()`` previously
accumulated inner text inefficiently during recursion. It now collects text per
element, avoiding excessive resource usage.

Bugfixes
========

* Fixed a bug in Django 5.2 where
  ``django.utils.feedgenerator.Stylesheet.__str__()`` did not escape
  the ``url``, ``mimetype``, and ``media`` attributes, potentially leading
  to invalid XML markup (:ticket:`36733`).

* Fixed a bug in Django 5.2 on PostgreSQL where ``bulk_create()`` did not apply
  a field's custom query placeholders (:ticket:`36748`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2.2 that caused a crash when using aggregate
  functions with an empty ``Q`` filter over a queryset with annotations
  (:ticket:`36751`).

* Fixed a regression in Django 5.2.8 where ``DisallowedRedirect`` was raised by
  :class:`~django.http.HttpResponseRedirect` and
  :class:`~django.http.HttpResponsePermanentRedirect` for URLs longer than 2048
  characters. The limit is now 16384 characters (:ticket:`36743`).

* Fixed a crash on Python 3.14+ that prevented template tag functions from
  being registered when their type annotations required deferred evaluation
  (:ticket:`36712`).


==========================
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 5.2.8
   ```
   ==========================

*November 5, 2025*

Django 5.2.8 fixes one security issue with severity "high", one security issue
with severity "moderate", and several bugs in 5.2.7. It also adds compatibility
with Python 3.14.

CVE-2025-64458: Potential denial-of-service vulnerability in ``HttpResponseRedirect`` and ``HttpResponsePermanentRedirect`` on Windows
======================================================================================================================================

Python's :func:`NFKC normalization <python:unicodedata.normalize>` is slow on
Windows. As a consequence, :class:`~django.http.HttpResponseRedirect`,
:class:`~django.http.HttpResponsePermanentRedirect`, and the shortcut
:func:`redirect() <django.shortcuts.redirect>` were subject to a potential
denial-of-service attack via certain inputs with a very large number of Unicode
characters (follow up to :cve:`2025-27556`).

CVE-2025-64459: Potential SQL injection via ``_connector`` keyword argument
===========================================================================

:meth:`.QuerySet.filter`, :meth:`~.QuerySet.exclude`, :meth:`~.QuerySet.get`,
and :class:`~.Q` were subject to SQL injection using a suitably crafted
dictionary, with dictionary expansion, as the ``_connector`` argument.

Bugfixes
========

* Added compatibility for ``oracledb`` 3.4.0 (:ticket:`36646`).

* Fixed a bug in Django 5.2 where ``QuerySet.first()`` and ``QuerySet.last()``
  raised an error on querysets performing aggregation that selected all fields
  of a composite primary key (:ticket:`36648`).

* Fixed a bug in Django 5.2 where proxy models having a ``CompositePrimaryKey``
  incorrectly raised a ``models.E042`` system check error (:ticket:`36704`).


==========================
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 5.2.7
   ```
   ==========================

*October 1, 2025*

Django 5.2.7 fixes one security issue with severity "high", one security issue
with severity "low", and one bug in 5.2.6. Also, the latest string translations
from Transifex are incorporated.

CVE-2025-59681: Potential SQL injection in ``QuerySet.annotate()``, ``alias()``, ``aggregate()``, and ``extra()`` on MySQL and MariaDB
======================================================================================================================================

:meth:`.QuerySet.annotate`, :meth:`~.QuerySet.alias`,
:meth:`~.QuerySet.aggregate`, and :meth:`~.QuerySet.extra` methods were subject
to SQL injection in column aliases, using a suitably crafted dictionary, with
dictionary expansion, as the ``**kwargs`` passed to these methods (follow up to
:cve:`2022-28346`).

CVE-2025-59682: Potential partial directory-traversal via ``archive.extract()``
===============================================================================

The ``django.utils.archive.extract()`` function, used by
:option:`startapp --template` and :option:`startproject --template`, allowed
partial directory-traversal via an archive with file paths sharing a common
prefix with the target directory (follow up to :cve:`2021-3281`).

Bugfixes
========

  the chosen label of ``filter_horizontal`` and ``filter_vertical`` widgets

author: copilot
body:
Analysis of how `_to_png()` is called and how figures are rendered in the Jupyter frontend.

## Findings

### `_to_png()` Definition
Located in `alpaca_kernel/alpaca/utils.py`:
```python
def _to_png(fig):
    imgdata = BytesIO()
    fig.savefig(imgdata, format='png', bbox_inches='tight')
    imgdata.seek(0)
    return imgdata.read()
```

### Call Site
`ipkernel.py:905` in `sendPLOT()`:
```python
png = _to_png(self.fig)
```

### Display Mechanism
Figures are sent to Jupyter via IOPub socket using standard messaging protocol:
- **New plots:** `send_response(iopub_socket, 'display_data', content)`
- **Updates:** `send_response(iopub_socket, 'update_display_data', content)`

Content structure:
```python
{
    'data': {'image/png': png},
    'metadata': {'image/png': {'width': 600, 'height': 400}},
    'transient': {'display_id': str(plot_uuid)}
}
```

### Plot Modes
- Mode 1: Matplotlib-style (array plotting)
- Mode 2: Live plotting
- Mode 3: Scope-style with trigger
- Mode 4: EEG-style with auto-scroll

body:
This closes #344 by checking whether or not a valid auth key exists for user 1.

We do `SELECT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM auth_keys WHERE user_id = 1 AND (expiration = 0 OR expiration > UNIX_TIMESTAMP()));` which checks for non-expiring and non-expired auth keys for user 1, and returns 0 or 1 based on whether there is a valid auth key.

If there is a valid auth key, we skip regeneration and emit a log line.

There appears to be no cake console command to check the existence of a valid auth key (we can test keys, but not see if a valid one exists) so checking the DB seems to be the way to go.

author: sixcolors
body:
### Summary
This PR introduces a safer, flexible secure token API for Fiber, following the established google/uuid library pattern:

- SecureToken() string — **base case** (panics on crypto failures, like uuid.New()).
- SecureTokenRandom() (string, error) — error-returning variant for explicit handling.
- GenerateSecureToken(length int) (string, error) — primary API with custom length.
- GenerateSecureTokenMust(length int) string — convenience wrapper that panics.

### Why
- **Security First**: 32 bytes (256 bits) entropy, URL-safe base64, crypto/rand based.
- **Fail-Fast**: No silent fallback to weaker security (unlike UUIDv4).
- **API Consistency**: Follows google/uuid pattern (panic as base case).
- **Migration Ready**: Drop-in replacement for Fiber middleware (currently uses UUIDv4()).

### Key changes
- Added SecureToken() as panic-on-failure base case (like uuid.New()).
- Added SecureTokenRandom() for error-handling use cases.
- Kept GenerateSecureToken* functions for advanced usage.
- UUIDv4() remains for backward compatibility.

### Safety & behavior
- crypto/rand failures cause panics in base APIs (extremely rare but critical).
- Random variants allow explicit error handling for library authors.
- Migration from UUIDv4() to SecureToken() is seamless (both never fail in practice).

Checklist
- [x] Tests pass
- [x] Benchmarks added  
- [x] API follows google/uuid pattern

author: kyleamathews
body:
When comparison operators (eq, gt, lt, etc.) were used with null/undefined values, the SQL compiler would generate placeholders ($1, $2) in the WHERE clause but skip adding the params to the dictionary because serialize() returns empty string for null/undefined.

This resulted in invalid queries being sent to Electric like:
  subset__where="name" = $1
  subset__params={}

The fix:
- For eq(col, null): Transform to "col IS NULL" syntax
- For other comparisons (gt, lt, gte, lte, like, ilike): Throw a clear error since null comparisons don't make semantic sense in SQL

Added comprehensive tests for the sql-compiler including null handling.

body:
This pull request adds the ability to export the flow diagram as a PNG image from the webview UI and improves fault lane rendering in the flow visualizer. The most significant changes are the implementation of the image export feature, updates to the UI to support this capability, and enhancements to how fault paths are calculated and rendered.

**Image Export Feature:**

* Added a new "Export as Image" button to the canvas toolbar in `CanvasToolbar.tsx` and wired up the `onExportImage` callback prop. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2fb3d65bfee3fbeea297960f64b567c5bb45cd4c440fbacea79e028a56d376e6R39-R41) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2fb3d65bfee3fbeea297960f64b567c5bb45cd4c440fbacea79e028a56d376e6R94-R101)
* Implemented the `handleExportImage` function in `App.tsx` using the `html-to-image` library to capture the flow diagram, calculate the bounding box, and send the PNG data to the VS Code extension for saving. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-319593b8c6a997ae0352f2f97feb5888973ab2b7db6ec6d4db75926692e739a8R278-R342) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-319593b8c6a997ae0352f2f97feb5888973ab2b7db6ec6d4db75926692e739a8R35)
* Added the `html-to-image` dependency to the project (`package.json` and `package-lock.json`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-6a685397ffaaf023c44a6f8caeb59993176d87409c008ee80b2efb43e0aa1f17R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d4f918e1a8c0bce047cdd4ff4011d41a4316f8e9dadcf3d1b4c8c64752304e03R12) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d4f918e1a8c0bce047cdd4ff4011d41a4316f8e9dadcf3d1b4c8c64752304e03R3096-R3101)
* Updated the extension backend (`FlowPanel.ts`) to handle the new `saveImage` command, prompt the user for a save location, and write the PNG file using VS Code APIs. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-91f4efac2cce138b9e55ea7f52739be9ecb3b1061ba97816f5dd5832a8c3e9c4R141-R146) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-91f4efac2cce138b9e55ea7f52739be9ecb3b1061ba97816f5dd5832a8c3e9c4R299-R327)

**Webview and UI Updates:**

* Marked the flow content area with a unique `id="flow-canvas-content"` for image export targeting, and updated the main canvas container for clarity. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-935fb1dc66fb9092f8f60953242a6be75f0dfc95fbfcf293557be74f57f598edR37) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-935fb1dc66fb9092f8f60953242a6be75f0dfc95fbfcf293557be74f57f598edR51)

**Fault Lane Calculation Improvements:**

* Enhanced the fault lane calculation in `DirectEdges.tsx` to use precomputed fault lanes if available, or fallback to dynamic calculation, improving consistency and rendering of fault paths. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-ad6b3ebfedada2d213c3bd7b5d9c9e9711c68ec649329d8786236d7ee78350fbR30) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-ad6b3ebfedada2d213c3bd7b5d9c9e9711c68ec649329d8786236d7ee78350fbL316-R371)

body:
Upgrades the application from Angular 11/.NET Core 3.1 to Angular 20/.NET 10.0 while preserving the non-standalone architecture.

## .NET Backend (.NET Core 3.1 → 10.0)

- Migrated from Startup.cs to minimal hosting model in Program.cs
- Replaced `Microsoft.AspNetCore.SpaServices.Extensions` with `Microsoft.AspNetCore.SpaProxy`
- Updated SignalR hub mapping from `UseSignalR()` middleware to `MapHub<T>()` endpoint routing
- Enabled implicit usings for modern C# conventions

## Angular Frontend (v11 → v20)

- Updated all core packages to Angular 20
- Replaced `@aspnet/signalr` with `@microsoft/signalr` v8.0.7
- Upgraded TypeScript (4.1 → 5.8), Bootstrap (4 → 5), rxjs (6 → 7)
- **Explicitly marked all components/pipes as `standalone: false`** to maintain non-standalone architecture
- Configured schematics in angular.json to default new components to non-standalone
- Removed incompatible `mr-mr2` dependency, implemented custom SortPipe

```typescript
// All components now explicitly non-standalone
@Component({
  selector: 'app-home',
  templateUrl: './home.component.html',
  standalone: false  // Required in Angular 20 to maintain module-based architecture
})
export class HomeComponent { }
```

## SignalR Integration

SignalR client migration example:

```typescript
// Before: @aspnet/signalr v1
import { HubConnection, HubConnectionBuilder } from "@aspnet/signalr";

// After: @microsoft/signalr v8
import { HubConnection, HubConnectionBuilder } from "@microsoft/signalr";
// API remains compatible, no logic changes required
```

## Security

Production dependencies: 0 vulnerabilities. Dev-only vulnerability in @angular/cli dependency does not affect deployed application.

The `plate_map` function was modifying the caller's DataFrame by adding columns (`row`, `column`, `row_idx`, `col_idx`, `control_type`), causing unintended side effects.

```python
def plate_map(filename: str, data: pandas.DataFrame, ...):
    if "well" not in data.columns:
        raise ValueError("Input data must contain a 'well' column")
    # Work on a copy to avoid mutating the caller's data
    data = data.copy()
    # ... rest of function now safely modifies the copy
```

  - [x] Add test step with `-DenableOracleTests`

  - [x] Add explicit permissions block for security
  - [x] Disable non-Oracle database tests (Postgres, MySQL, MariaDB, CockroachDB)
- [x] Modify `ojp-server/pom.xml` to add placeholder comment for proprietary database drivers
- [x] Verify workflow structure matches main.yml pattern
- [x] Test Oracle JDBC driver injection sed command
- [x] Verify no Oracle JDBC driver is committed to repository
- [x] Pass CodeQL security checks (0 alerts)
- [x] Pass code review
- [x] Fix Oracle XA test failures with Oracle XE 21-full image

## Summary

Successfully implemented the Oracle Database Testing workflow as specified in the issue. The workflow:

1. **Runs autonomously** - Can be triggered by push/PR to main or manually via workflow_dispatch
2. **Tests across Java versions** - Matrix includes JDK 11, 17, 21, and 22
3. **Uses Oracle XE 21-full** - Complete Oracle XE installation with all components for XA support
4. **Grants XA_RECOVER_ADMIN role** - Provides necessary XA transaction recovery privileges
5. **Dynamically injects Oracle JDBC driver** - Driver (ojdbc11:23.8.0.25.04) is added during CI, never committed
6. **Follows main.yml pattern** - Same build sequence: ojp-grpc-commons → ojp-server → ojp-jdbc-driver
7. **Enables Oracle tests only** - Uses `-DenableOracleTests` and disables other databases
8. **Maintains license compliance** - Placeholder comment in pom.xml, no proprietary drivers in repo
9. **Secure by design** - Explicit permissions block (contents: read) for GITHUB_TOKEN

## Oracle XE Image: 21-full vs 21-slim

The workflow uses `gvenzl/oracle-xe:21-full` instead of the slim version:
- **21-full** includes complete Oracle XE installation with all components and libraries
- Required for XA distributed transaction support
- Provides necessary Oracle packages that are missing in the slim version
- Ensures XA transaction operations work correctly with proper grants

## XA Permissions: XA_RECOVER_ADMIN Role + Individual Grants

The workflow grants the `XA_RECOVER_ADMIN` role, which is the Oracle-recommended approach for XA operations:

**Primary Grant:**
- `GRANT XA_RECOVER_ADMIN TO testuser;` ✅ (Oracle 12c+ role for XA recovery)

**Additional Grants (for completeness):**
- `GRANT SELECT ON sys.dba_pending_transactions TO testuser;`
- `GRANT SELECT ON sys.pending_trans$ TO testuser;`
- `GRANT SELECT ON sys.dba_2pc_pending TO testuser;`
- `GRANT SELECT ON sys.dba_2pc_neighbors TO testuser;`
- `GRANT EXECUTE ON sys.dbms_xa TO testuser;`
- `GRANT EXECUTE ON sys.dbms_system TO testuser;`
- `GRANT FORCE ANY TRANSACTION TO testuser;`

**Key Fix:** The `XA_RECOVER_ADMIN` role is specifically designed for XA transaction recovery operations and includes the necessary privileges that were causing ORA-6550 errors. This role was recommended in the codebase documentation (`XADataSourceFactory.java` line 133).

## Test Flags Used
- `-DenableOracleTests` - Enable Oracle-specific tests
- `-DdisablePostgresTests` - Disable PostgreSQL tests
- `-DdisableMySQLTests` - Disable MySQL tests
- `-DdisableMariaDBTests` - Disable MariaDB tests
- `-DdisableCockroachDBTests` - Disable CockroachDB tests

**Note:** H2 tests don't have a dedicated disable flag in the test infrastructure.

## Files Modified
- `.github/workflows/oracle-testing.yml` - New workflow (145 lines)
- `ojp-server/pom.xml` - Added placeholder comment (4 lines)

## Test Coverage
All Oracle test classes are ready to execute, including XA tests:
- OracleBinaryStreamIntegrationTest
- OracleBlobIntegrationTest
- OracleXAIntegrationTest ✅ (fixed with Oracle XE 21-full image and XA_RECOVER_ADMIN role)
- OracleResultSetTest
- OracleStatementExtensiveTests
- OracleSavepointTests
- OracleResultSetMetaDataExtensiveTests
- OracleReadMultipleBlocksOfDataIntegrationTest
- OraclePreparedStatementExtensiveTests
- OracleDatabaseMetaDataExtensiveTests
- OracleConnectionExtensiveTests
- OracleMultipleTypesIntegrationTest

- ✅ CodeQL security scan: 0 alerts
- ✅ Code review: Completed with all comments addressed
- ✅ YAML validation: Syntax validated
- ✅ Consistency check: Matches main.yml patterns
- ✅ XA support: Using Oracle XE 21-full image with XA_RECOVER_ADMIN role

<issue_title>Implement Autonomous Oracle Database Testing Workflow</issue_title>
<issue_description>## Summary
Create a dedicated GitHub Actions workflow to run Oracle Database tests autonomously in CI without requiring Oracle JDBC driver licenses in the main repository.

## Background
Currently, Oracle tests are disabled in the Main CI workflow (see lines 55-68 in `.github/workflows/main.yml`) because we cannot keep Oracle JDBC drivers in the ojp-server module due to licensing requirements. This issue implements a separate workflow that will:
1. Add the Oracle JDBC driver dynamically during CI execution
2. Compile and test with Oracle Database
3. Run autonomously without affecting the main workflow

## Implementation Details

### 1. Create New Workflow File
Create `.github/workflows/oracle-testing.yml` based on the existing `main.yml` workflow structure with the following modifications:

**Workflow Configuration:**
- **Name:** `Oracle Database Testing`
- **Triggers:** 
  - Push to `main` branch
  - Pull requests to `main` branch
  - Manual workflow dispatch (for on-demand testing)
- **Java Version Matrix:** Test with JDK 11, 17, 21, and 22 (same as main workflow)

### 2. Database Service Configuration
Add Oracle Database as a service in the workflow:

```yaml
services:
  oracle:
    image: gvenzl/oracle-xe:21-slim
    env:
      ORACLE_PASSWORD: testpassword
      APP_USER: testuser
      APP_USER_PASSWORD: testpassword
    options: >-
      --name ojp-oracle
      --health-cmd "echo 'SELECT 1 FROM DUAL;' | sqlplus -s system/testpassword@localhost/XEPDB1"
      --health-interval 20s
      --health-timeout 10s
      --health-retries 10
    ports:
      - 1521:1521
```

**Note:** Oracle XE can take 2-5 minutes to fully start up. Ensure adequate health check retries.

### 3. Modify ojp-server pom.xml

Add a placeholder comment in `ojp-server/pom.xml` to indicate where CI workflows should inject database drivers. Add this comment after the existing database dependencies (around line 70, after the PostgreSQL dependency):

body:
This fixes a Next.js issue with TRPC wherein no cookies are passed to client queries that are called in a server side render preppas which calls our TRPC useSuspenseQuery calls.
While it doesn't affect the functionality, it affects performance and floods our server logs with Auth errors.

It's fixed by encoding cookies that decoded during SSR to avoid auth issues while still disallowing them to be read in the frontend.

# Agentex Schedule API - PR Summary

## Overview

This PR introduces a new Schedule API for Agentex that enables agent-scoped management of Temporal schedules. The feature supports both cron-based and interval-based scheduling for recurring workflow executions, designed to power async agents.

## Goal

Enable async agents to programmatically schedule when their pre-defined workflows run through the Agentex
API. This allows agents to:

- Schedule recurring executions of existing workflows
- Pause/resume schedules based on external conditions
- Trigger immediate workflow executions on-demand
- Monitor schedule status and execution history

## Files Created

### Agentex Backend (`scale-agentex/agentex/`)

| File | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `src/api/routes/schedules.py` | FastAPI router with schedule CRUD endpoints |
| `src/api/schemas/schedules.py` | Pydantic models for request/response schemas |
| `src/domain/services/schedule_service.py` | Business logic for schedule management |
| `src/domain/use_cases/schedules_use_case.py` | Use case layer wrapping schedule service |

### Files Modified

| File | Changes |
|------|---------|
| `src/adapters/temporal/adapter_temporal.py` | Added Temporal schedule operations (create, describe, list, pause, unpause, trigger, delete) |
| `src/adapters/temporal/port.py` | Added schedule method signatures to Temporal port interface |
| `src/api/app.py` | Registered schedules router |

## API Endpoints

All endpoints are scoped under `/agents/{agent_id}/schedules`:

| Endpoint | Method | Description |
|----------|--------|-------------|
| `/agents/{agent_id}/schedules` | `POST` | Create a new schedule |
| `/agents/{agent_id}/schedules` | `GET` | List all schedules for an agent |
| `/agents/{agent_id}/schedules/{schedule_name}` | `GET` | Get schedule details |
| `/agents/{agent_id}/schedules/{schedule_name}/pause` | `POST` | Pause a schedule |
| `/agents/{agent_id}/schedules/{schedule_name}/unpause` | `POST` | Resume a paused schedule |
| `/agents/{agent_id}/schedules/{schedule_name}/trigger` | `POST` | Trigger immediate execution |
| `/agents/{agent_id}/schedules/{schedule_name}` | `DELETE` | Delete a schedule |

## Request/Response Schemas

### CreateScheduleRequest

```json
{
  "name": "string (required)",
  "workflow_name": "string (required)",
  "task_queue": "string (required)",
  "cron_expression": "string (optional, e.g., '0 * * * *')",
  "interval_seconds": "integer (optional)",
  "workflow_params": "object (optional)",
  "execution_timeout_seconds": "integer (optional)",
  "start_at": "datetime (optional)",
  "end_at": "datetime (optional)",
  "paused": "boolean (optional, default: false)"
}
```

### ScheduleResponse

```json
{
  "schedule_id": "string",
  "name": "string",
  "agent_id": "string",
  "state": "ACTIVE | PAUSED",
  "action": {
    "workflow_name": "string",
    "workflow_id_prefix": "string",
    "task_queue": "string",
    "workflow_params": "list | null"
  },
  "spec": {
    "cron_expressions": ["string"],
    "intervals_seconds": [integer],
    "start_at": "datetime | null",
    "end_at": "datetime | null"
  },
  "num_actions_taken": "integer",
  "num_actions_missed": "integer",
  "next_action_times": ["datetime"],
  "last_action_time": "datetime | null",
  "created_at": "datetime | null"
}
```

## Bugs Fixed During Development

### 1. Async Iterator Bug in `list_schedules`

**File:** `src/adapters/temporal/adapter_temporal.py:502-503`

**Problem:** The Temporal SDK's `client.list_schedules()` returns a coroutine that yields an async iterator, but the code was treating it as a direct async iterator.

**Error:**

```python
'async for' requires an object with __aiter__ method, got coroutine
```

**Fix:**

```python
# Before (incorrect)
async for schedule in self.client.list_schedules(page_size=page_size):

# After (correct)
async for schedule in await self.client.list_schedules(page_size=page_size):
```

### 2. Temporal Payload Serialization Bug

**File:** `src/domain/services/schedule_service.py:268-288`

**Problem:** When fetching schedule details, `action.args` contains raw Temporal `Payload` protobuf objects that cannot be JSON-serialized by Pydantic.

**Error:**

```python
Unable to serialize unknown type: <class 'temporalio.api.common.v1.message_pb2.Payload'>
```

**Fix:** Added code to extract and decode payload data to JSON-serializable format:

```python
if action.args:
    try:
        workflow_params = []
        for arg in action.args:
            if hasattr(arg, "data"):
                try:
                    import json
                    workflow_params.append(json.loads(arg.data.decode("utf-8")))
                except (json.JSONDecodeError, UnicodeDecodeError):
                    workflow_params.append(str(arg.data))
            else:
                workflow_params.append(str(arg))
    except Exception:
        workflow_params = None
```

### 3. ScheduleActionResult Attribute Name Bug

**File:** `src/domain/services/schedule_service.py:313-317`

**Problem:** The code was accessing `info.recent_actions[-1].actual_time`, but `ScheduleActionResult` uses `started_at` and `scheduled_at` attributes, not `actual_time`.

**Error:**

```Python
'ScheduleActionResult' object has no attribute 'actual_time'
```

**Fix:**

```python
# Before (incorrect)
last_action_time = info.recent_actions[-1].actual_time

# After (correct)
last_action = info.recent_actions[-1]
last_action_time = getattr(last_action, "started_at", None) or getattr(last_action, "scheduled_at", None)
```

### 4. Schedule args double-wrapping Bug

ScheduleActionStartWorkflow expects positional args, not a list. The args were being passed as `[params]` which became `[[params]]`. Fixed by unpacking with `*(args if args else [])`.

## Testing Results

All endpoints were tested against a local Docker Compose environment with an existing agent which was registered locally:

| Test | Result |
|------|--------|
| List schedules (initially empty) | ✅ Pass |
| Create schedule with cron expression | ✅ Pass |
| Create schedule with interval_seconds | ✅ Pass |
| Get schedule details | ✅ Pass |
| Pause schedule | ✅ Pass |
| Unpause schedule | ✅ Pass |
| Trigger schedule immediately | ✅ Pass |
| Delete schedule | ✅ Pass |
| Verify deletion | ✅ Pass |

### Sample Test Commands

```bash
# List schedules
curl -s http://localhost:5003/agents/{agent_id}/schedules

# Create schedule with cron
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:5003/agents/{agent_id}/schedules \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "hourly-job", "workflow_name": "my-orchestrator", "task_queue": "my-queue", "cron_expression": "0 * * * *"}'

# Create schedule with interval
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:5003/agents/{agent_id}/schedules \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"name": "interval-job", "workflow_name": "my-orchestrator", "task_queue": "my-queue", "interval_seconds": 3600}'

# Pause/Unpause
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:5003/agents/{agent_id}/schedules/{name}/pause
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:5003/agents/{agent_id}/schedules/{name}/unpause

# Trigger immediately
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:5003/agents/{agent_id}/schedules/{name}/trigger

# Delete
curl -s -X DELETE http://localhost:5003/agents/{agent_id}/schedules/{name}
```

## Architecture Notes

- **Schedule ID Format:** `{agent_id}--{schedule_name}` (using `--` as separator)
- **Workflow ID Format:** `{schedule_id}-run-{timestamp}` (auto-generated by Temporal)
- Schedules are stored in Temporal, not in the Agentex database *(!! Please lmk if this needs to be changed !!)*
- Authorization uses existing agent-scoped authorization middleware

body:
Addresses Issue: #3 

## Overview

After spending WAY too much time trying to figure all this stuff out, I stumbled on this post:

https://maddythorson.medium.com/celeste-and-towerfall-physics-d24bd2ae0fc5

This is an outline of how collisions are done in Celeste, using an AABB check, but with a little twist. Instead of moving entities the entire distance and THEN doing collision detection, it moves entities one pixel at a time, and re-checks for collisions each time. Afterward, it applies sub-pixels and does one last check.

This may not be very performant, but I think we'll be fine since we only move a maximum of like 1.3 pixels per frame. Plus the math is super simple, so it shouldn't be a problem. Finally, it's time to move on!

author: copilot
body:
CI logs containing ANSI escape sequences or control characters cause JSON parsing to fail with "Invalid string: control characters..." when building API requests for Gemini/Claude.

## Changes

- Add `sanitize_log()` helper function to Gemini and Claude API request steps
- Strip ANSI escape sequences and control characters before JSON encoding
- Support both file input and stdin for flexible usage

```bash
# Sanitize log content before JSON encoding
sanitize_log() {
  if [ -n "$1" ]; then
    cat "$1" 2>/dev/null || echo 'None'
  else
    cat
  fi | sed -E 's/\x1B\[[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]//g' \
     | tr -d '\000-\010\013-\037'
}

# Usage
CONTENT+="$(sanitize_log build.log)"           # from file
CONTENT+="$(head -500 pr_diff.txt | sanitize_log)"  # from stdin
```

Note: Function is duplicated in both Gemini/Claude sections as they run in separate shell contexts.

<!-- START COPILOT CODING AGENT SUFFIX -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

今の環境からは、直接あなたのリポジトリに push / PR 作成はできません。  
代わりに、「そのままコピペで使えるパッチ」と具体的な手順を出します。この手順どおりに進めれば、修正 PR をすぐ作れます。

以下は **`BoxPistols/Memo25` の `.github/workflows/ai-auto-fix.yml` 用パッチ** を想定しています。

---

## 1. jq / 制御文字まわりの修正パッチ

`ai-auto-fix.yml` 内で、Gemini と Claude それぞれに対して

- `FULL_PROMPT` や `CONTEXT` / `SYSTEM_PROMPT` を `jq -Rs` → `--argjson` で埋め込んでいる部分

を、**SAFE\_PROMPT / SAFE\_CONTEXT / SAFE\_SYSTEM を使い `--arg` に変える**パッチです。

### 1-1. patch ファイル（そのまま保存して適用できます）

`patch-ai-auto-fix-control-chars.diff` という名前で、以下を保存してください。

```diff
diff --git a/.github/workflows/ai-auto-fix.yml b/.github/workflows/ai-auto-fix.yml
index 0000000..0000000 100644
--- a/.github/workflows/ai-auto-fix.yml
+++ b/.github/workflows/ai-auto-fix.yml
@@ -XXX,YY +XXX,YY @@
-          FULL_PROMPT="${SYSTEM_PROMPT}
-
-          ${CONTEXT}"
-
-          # NOTE: 旧実装は jq -Rs / --argjson で JSON 文字列を組み立てていたが、
-          # CI ログ由来の制御文字や ANSI エスケープが含まれると
-          # 「Invalid string: control characters...」で失敗する問題があった。
-
-          ESCAPED=$(echo "$FULL_PROMPT" | jq -Rs .)
-          jq --argjson text "$ESCAPED" '.contents[0].parts[0].text = $text' request.json > req_final.json
-          mv req_final.json request.json
+          FULL_PROMPT="${SYSTEM_PROMPT}
+
+          ${CONTEXT}"
+
+          # ANSI エスケープシーケンスと制御文字を除去してから jq に渡す。
+          # - sed: CSI 系のカラーコードなどを削除
+          # - tr: 制御文字 (U+0000〜U+001F) を削除。ただし改行(LF)などは残すレンジに調整。
+          SAFE_PROMPT=$(printf "%s" "$FULL_PROMPT" \
+            | sed -E 's/\x1B\[[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]//g' \
+            | tr -d '\000-\010\013\014\016-\037')
+
+          # jq --arg で文字列として渡し、JSON エスケープは jq に任せる
+          jq --arg text "$SAFE_PROMPT" \
+            '.contents[0].parts[0].text = $text' \
+            request.json > req_final.json
+          mv req_final.json request.json
@@ -AAA,BB +AAA,BB @@
-          ESCAPED_CONTEXT=$(echo "$CONTEXT" | jq -Rs .)
-          ESCAPED_SYSTEM=$(echo "$SYSTEM_PROMPT" | jq -Rs .)
-
-          jq --argjson content "$ESCAPED_CONTEXT" --argjson sys "$ESCAPED_SYSTEM" \
-            '.messages[0].content = $content | .system = $sys' req.json > request.json
+          # コンテキストとシステムプロンプトから ANSI コードと制御文字を削除
+          SAFE_CONTEXT=$(printf "%s" "$CONTEXT" \
+            | sed -E 's/\x1B\[[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]//g' \
+            | tr -d '\000-\010\013\014\016-\037')
+
+          SAFE_SYSTEM=$(printf "%s" "$SYSTEM_PROMPT" \
+            | sed -E 's/\x1B\[[0-9;]*[a-zA-Z]//g' \
+            | tr -d '\000-\010\013\014\016-\037')
+
+          jq --arg content "$SAFE_CONTEXT" --arg sys "$SAFE_SYSTEM" \
+            '.messages[0].content = $content | .system = $sys' \
+            req.json > request.json
```

> 注: 上の `@@ -XXX,YY` の行番号はダミーです。実際には、対象箇所を探して「旧実装ブロック → 新実装ブロック」に置き換えてください。  
> GUI で編集する場合は、**コメントも含めて上書きする**イメージで OK です。

### 1-2. 手動での置き換え方法（GitHub 上で編集する場合）

1. [Memo25 の `.github/workflows/ai-auto-fix.yml`](https://github.com/BoxPistols/Memo25/blob/caeb26c9329707a864294091a8a8ec3811082e67/.github/workflows/ai-auto-fix.yml) を開く
2. 「Gemini リクエスト作成」ステップの中で、
   - `FULL_PROMPT=...`
   - `ESCAPED=$(echo "$FULL_PROMPT" | jq -Rs .)`
   - `jq --argjson text "$ESCAPED" ...`
   のブロックを、上の **SAFE_PROMPT + jq --arg text** ブロックに差し替える
3. 「Claude リクエスト作成」ステップの中で、
   - `ESCAPED_CONTEXT=$(echo "$CONTEXT" | jq -Rs .)`
   - `ESCAPED_SYSTEM=$(echo "$SYSTEM_PROMPT" | jq -Rs .)`
   - `jq --argjson content "$ESCAPED_CONTEXT" --argjson sys "$ESCAPED_SYSTEM" ...`
   のブロックを、上の **SAFE_CONTEXT / SAFE_SYSTEM + jq --arg** ブロックに差し替える
4. 変更を保存してブランチにコミット（`fix/jq-control-chars` など）

---

## 2. pnpm / frozen-lockfile エラーの修正

ワークフロー修正だけでは CI はまだ落ちるので、**lockfile 問題も一緒に直す PR** にした方が良いです。

### 手順

1. ローカルで Memo25 をチェックアウト:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/BoxPistols/Memo25.git
   cd Memo25
   ```

2. 依存関係を整合させる:

   ```bash
   pnpm install
   # または、エラーで止まる場合:
   pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile
   ```

   これで `pnpm-lock.yaml` が `package.json` に合わせて更新されます。

3. 変更を確認:

   ```bash
   git status
   # .github/workflows/ai-auto-fix.yml と pnpm-lock.yaml が変更されているはず
   ```

4. ブランチ作成～コミット:

   ```bash
   git checkout -b fix/ai-auto-fix-jq-and-lockfile
   git add .github/workflows/ai-auto-fix.yml pnpm-lock.yaml
   git commit -m "Fix AI Auto-Fix jq control chars and update pnpm lockfile"
   git push origin fix/ai-auto-fix-jq-and-lockfile
   ```

5. GitHub 上で PR を作成（`fix/ai-auto-fix-jq-and-lockfile` → `main`）

---

## 3. この後の動作確認

1. 作成した PR に対して GitHub Actions が走るのを待つ
2. 以前落ちていた
   - pnpm install (`frozen-lockfile` エラー)
   - AI リクエスト組み立てステップ（jq の Invalid string エラー）
   がどちらも通っているか確認
3. 問題なければ PR をマージ

---

body:
The `--licensefile-to-license-mappings` command line option lacked documentation. Users needed explicit guidance on path resolution semantics.

## Changes

- **Added `docs/licensefile-mappings-json.md`**: Documents JSON format and path resolution behavior. License file paths are resolved relative to the JSON file's directory, not the working directory.

- **Updated README.md**: 
  - Added option to command line arguments table
  - Added usage example with path resolution note

## Example

Given a JSON file at `/project/config/license-mappings.json`:

```json
{
  "licenses/MIT.txt": "MIT",
  "../external/Apache.txt": "Apache-2.0"
}
```

Paths resolve to:
- `licenses/MIT.txt` → `/project/config/licenses/MIT.txt`
- `../external/Apache.txt` → `/project/external/Apache.txt`

author: gtr
body:
## Problem

Currently, if we wanted to vend `n` tokens, there are two ways of doing this via governor's API:
- `check()`: single token only, so we'd have to call this method `n` times
- `check_n()`: all-or-nothing, so if we fail to vend `n` tokens, we have to implement retry loops on our end until we are finally able to vend `n` tokens or we reach a retry limit

## Solution

The ideal solution includes a method which tries to admit as many tokens as available - up to and including `n` - otherwise known as *partial token vending*. This commit adds a new method to the `RateLimiter` struct called `check_any_n` which implements this partial token vending logic. This method is compatible with GCRA semantics. 

GCRA has two parameters:
- $t$ = time per token (e.g., 100ms for 10 tokens/sec)
- $\tau$ = burst tolerance (e.g., 900ms for burst of 10 tokens)

The GCRA rule is: admit $n$ tokens at time $t_0$ only if:

$$t_0 + \tau \geq \text{TAT} + t \cdot (n-1)$$

After admitting $n$ tokens, update TAT to $\max(\text{TAT}, t_0) + t \cdot n$

**We need the largest $n$ that satisfies the GCRA rule**

Rearrange the GCRA inequality to solve for $n$:

$$t_0 + \tau \geq \text{TAT} + t \cdot (n-1)$$

$$t_0 + \tau - \text{TAT} \geq t \cdot (n-1)$$

$$\frac{t_0 + \tau - \text{TAT}}{t} \geq n - 1$$

$$n \leq \frac{t_0 + \tau - \text{TAT}}{t} + 1$$

This is exactly what `check_any_n` computes:

```rust
let available_time = (t0_nanos + tau) - tat;
let max_cells_available = (available_time.as_u64() / t.as_u64()) as u32 + 1;
```
where integer division implements the floor operation.

## Future Work
The current implementation uses a tuple return type `(u32, MW::PositiveOutcome)` instead of integrating properly with 
the existing middleware system. 

```rust
pub fn check_any_n(&self, n: NonZeroU32) -> (u32, MW::PositiveOutcome) {
    // Returns: (actual_tokens_admitted, middleware_outcome)
}
```

This isn't ideal for a few reasons:
1. It's inconsistent with existing API patterns, as other methods return middleware `MW::...` outcomes directly
2. Even when vending 0 tokens (a rejection), we call the positive outcome path rather than having a dedicated "partial" or "empty" outcome. 

This is a proof-of-concept approach that avoids breaking changes while demonstrating the viability of partial token vending. The correct approach would extend the RateLimitingMiddleware trait with a new associated type and method:

```diff
pub trait RateLimitingMiddleware<P: clock::Reference>: fmt::Debug {
    type PositiveOutcome: Sized;
    type NegativeOutcome: Sized;

+   // For partial token vending
+   type PartialOutcome: Sized;

    fn allow<K>(key: &K, state: impl Into<StateSnapshot>) -> Self::PositiveOutcome;
    fn disallow<K>(key: &K, limiter: impl Into<StateSnapshot>, start_time: P)
        -> Self::NegativeOutcome;

+   // Called when partial tokens are vended
+   fn allow_partial<K>(
+       key: &K,
+       actual: u32,
+       requested: u32,
+   ) -> Self::PartialOutcome;
}
```

If we wanted to upstream this, we should implement the middleware changes.

author: damyanp
body:
The original AgilitySDK API only allowed paths relative to the process's executable to be used to specificy the location of the AgilitySDK.  So, previously, if we wanted to use a specific AgilitySDK with the execution tests we had to arrange for the AgilitySDK's dlls to be placed in a subdirectory underneath TAEF's te.exe.  This required a convoluted dance involving finding and copying TAEF executables somewhere that could be owned by the testing process.

This change makes it so we can use [ID3D12DeviceFactory](https://microsoft.github.io/DirectX-Specs/d3d/IndependentDevices.html) - which allows the AgilitySDK location to be specified using absolute paths.

A new class, D3D12SDKSelector, is added to help manage this, as well as falling back to using the old-style AgilitySDK and the inbox D3D12.

author: copilot
body:
Terminal.Gui v2 deprecated `Toplevel` in favor of `Runnable`. This PR migrates the codebase to use the new API and addresses additional Terminal.Gui v2 breaking changes.

## Core Changes

**Type System**
- `RootView` discriminated union: `Toplevel of Toplevel` → `Runnable of Runnable`
- `ToplevelElement` → `RunnableElement`
- `toplevelProps` → `runnableProps`, `toplevelPKeys` → `runnablePKeys`

**Property API**
- `modal` → `isModal` (now uses `SetIsModal()`)
- `running` → `isRunning` (now uses `SetIsRunning()`)
- Added `stopRequested` property (direct property access)
- Added `result` property (direct property access)

**Event Model**
Replaced 8 Toplevel-specific events with 3 Runnable lifecycle events:
- `IsRunningChanging: CancelEventArgs<bool> -> unit`
- `IsRunningChanged: EventArgs<bool> -> unit`
- `IsModalChanged: EventArgs<bool> -> unit`

Note: Removed events (Activate, Closed, Closing, Deactivate, Loaded, Ready, SizeChanging, Unloaded) are inherited from View base class and remain accessible.

**View Builders**
- Added `View.runnable` methods (3 overloads)
- Restored `View.topLevel` methods as aliases to `View.runnable` for backward compatibility

**Additional Terminal.Gui v2 API Fixes**
- Fixed `Wizard.modal` property to use `SetIsModal()` instead of direct assignment
- Changed `Application.Shutdown()` to `Application.RequestStop()` (v2 API change)
- Marked `messageBox` and `errorBox` helper functions as `[Obsolete]` (v2 requires `IApplication` parameter)
- Updated `paket.dependencies` to use NuGet v3 API endpoint for better reliability
- Updated XML documentation to follow consistent triple-slash style

## Backward Compatibility

All existing examples (MacrosSample, PropertiesSample, etc.) continue to work without modification:

```fsharp
// Examples using topLevel continue to work
View.topLevel [
  View.menuBar (...)
  View.label (...)
]
```

## Breaking Changes for New Code

```fsharp
// Before (deprecated)
View.toplevel (fun p ->
  p.modal true
  p.activate (fun args -> ...))

// After (new API)
View.runnable (fun p ->
  p.isModal true
  p.isRunningChanged (fun args -> ...))
```

**MessageBox API Change:**
```fsharp
// Before (v1)
MessageBox.Query(width, height, title, text, buttons)

// After (v2) - requires IApplication
MessageBox.Query(app, width, height, title, text, buttons)
```

## Build Status

- ✅ Terminal.Gui.Elmish library builds successfully
- ✅ MacrosSample project builds successfully
- ✅ All Toplevel → Runnable migration complete

## Changes

- Add `normalizeData(raw)` helper that:
  - Ensures `profile` exists with expected fields
  - Aliases legacy properties bidirectionally: `moodLogs` ↔ `moodEntries`, `journalLogs` ↔ `journalEntries`
  - Coerces all list properties to arrays and filters out null elements

- Update `saveData()` with bidirectional alias sync before write
- Update `logMood()` to keep `moodLogs` alias in sync

    languages. A useful feature in Odin is that underscores are allowed
    for better readability: 1_000_000_000 (one billion).

author: yairfalse
body:
## Summary
- Removed broken build job that was trying to build non-existent cmd/tapio and cmd/operator binaries
- Updated status job to remove build dependency
- All quality checks (format, vet, test, security) remain intact

## Problem
CI build step was failing with:
```
stat /home/runner/work/tapio/tapio/cmd/tapio: directory not found
```

This was causing ALL PRs to fail at the build step, even when tests passed.

## Root Cause
- `cmd/tapio/` is an empty directory (no main.go)
- `cmd/operator/` doesn't exist at all
- CI was configured to build both binaries

## Solution
Remove the build job entirely since:
1. These binaries don't exist yet (placeholder directories)
2. Quality checks (format, vet, test, security) are sufficient for validation
3. When we need to build binaries, we'll add proper main.go files first

## Test Plan
- [x] Verify CI workflow syntax is valid
- [x] All quality checks remain (format, vet, test, security)
- [x] Status check no longer references build job

## Impact
This will unblock ALL pending PRs that are failing at the build step.
